title: adapter.facts@4
description: An agent's facts as data: the versions it covers, and per section what the core reads, each naming the core rule that reads it and its conformance case. No core rule branches on the agent's name; a new agent fills a file. @4 is @1 with the agent's own sandbox in a session DeepBuild starts, per version (`sandbox`), and how such a session launches (`launch.started`) (#1330); @2's install and @3's providers stay theirs.

started.description: How DeepBuild starts a session under your approval (#1330): args with {mode}, {settings}, {sandbox}, {worktree} and {prompt} filled; the mode that asks before acting; each mode a start may name and what fills {mode}; the modes that skip permission prompts; the variables that mark a nested session; the variable that names the account's home, and its default.

trust.description: Where the agent keeps folder trust as JSON, so the worktree a start made starts trusted: `file` with the default home, `homeFile` inside a home its variable names, and the dotted key `set` to true, {worktree} one key of it.

sandbox.description: The agent's own sandbox in a session DeepBuild starts (#1330), per version: the settings or config overrides that turn it on, the approval policy each mode takes under it, the walls it holds (writes, credentials, network; one not named is not held) and how its way out is turned off. A version not listed has none.

x-rules.rule: Who is calling: a subagent's stop or permission request is not its parent's, and another tool running the agent's hooks is not the agent; a session is owned by the adapter that bound its ID first.
Order by seq with ties by ID: a session's events sort by the seq deep-hook stamped, two with one seq by their IDs, and no two events share an ID.
A clock stepped back never moves an event before its turn started: the event keeps its arrival place, stamped no earlier than the turn's first event.
A late event in a stopped turn is recorded in that turn and reopens nothing: a PostToolUse after its turn's Stop changes nothing about how the turn ended.
When hooks go quiet the session reads unknown rather than finished; a wait is a lease, never a finish.
The session map threads across rotated IDs: a start after /clear, /compact or a fork names the thread it continues.
One owner per session: an answer reaches the session it was asked for and no other; another adapter only relays.
A permission answer takes allow only from decision, never from a suggestion or the text beside it.
A stop that can't be parsed read as unknown: a cause the facts don't list is unknown, never a listed cause and never a success.
Delivery confirmed from the transcript: an acknowledgement counts only with the transcript's sign of it.
